blockingFindings.title: Persistence drops real primary and FD-cleanup causes before aggregation
blockingFindings.expected: Preserve real primary and cleanup failures together, with primary as the causal root and cleanup separately available; do not replace both with cause-free placeholders.
blockingFindings.actual: Exclusive collision produces native EEXIST/open but returns a cause-free generic rejection. Invalidating only the new owned output FD makes native writeFile and FileHandle.close return EBADF/write and EBADF/close. Returned AggregateError contains only generic messages; both errors have no code, syscall, or cause. The native errors are absent from the causal graph.

reproduction.environment: Explicit scrubbed HOME/TMPDIR/config/cache as recorded in command artifacts; no credential variables. Script creates a fresh directory under its own temporary root on every run.
reproduction.boundary: Native filesystem syscalls. Node-only child uses real open, closeSync on its own newly-created FD, and transparent observation of actual FileHandle method failures. No fabricated Error replaces write/close.

blockingFindings.impact: Private helper violates its frozen failure-diagnostic contract; a pure AggregateError helper test cannot establish failure preservation at the persistence boundary.
blockingFindings.closure: Builder preserves actual causes/code through both catches, adds a regression through native filesystem/FD boundaries, and reruns unchanged relevant tests plus the red reproducer. No public/app/security-schema change needed.

blockingFindings.title: HTTP handler and close paths erase incoming errors before preservePrimaryError
blockingFindings.expected: Retain the actual handler failure, and preserve it alongside an eventual cleanup error when close rejects.
blockingFindings.actual: Delegating ServerResponse.writeHead to the real native method with invalid status creates ERR_HTTP_INVALID_STATUS_CODE. The handler catch discards it; close rejects with only "synthetic fault server: handler failed" and no cause/code. Exercising the actual close callback branch with a fake cleanup error after real successful native closure returns an AggregateError with two newly-created generic errors, retaining neither incoming cause.

reproduction.boundary: Real loopback request/handler and actual listener/socket closure; native Node RangeError induced through a test-only method interposition. Cleanup callback failure is synthetic, not an actual OS Server.close failure.

blockingFindings.impact: The aggregation utility preserves what it receives, but the actual lifecycle has already discarded the causes. Existing generated interruption-message coverage does not cover this contract.
blockingFindings.closure: Builder threads actual handler/server/response/close errors into preserved causal chains, with a test through the HTTP lifecycle rather than only preservePrimaryError. Keep current provider/gateway mapping and public sources unchanged.
